title: Lior and the Witness
premise: When the coffin of Lior Ashford, founder of the town of Witness, is exhumed for a land dispute and found empty, insurance investigator Juniper Pemberton discovers her own late mother's name forged on a thirty-year-old burial policy. Juniper's photographic memory lets her reconstruct the night of Lior's supposed death, revealing that the town's founding families staged it to cover his murder and smuggle his fortune out through fraudulent claims. As she closes in, she realizes her mother was the only witness who tried to stop them and died for it. In the end, Juniper exposes the conspiracy at the town's centennial gala, choosing justice outside the law over the settlement money offered to keep it buried, and finds belonging with the one founding-family descendant who helps her.
about_author: Petra Zhou is a former claims adjuster from the Pacific Northwest who spent a decade reading other people's disasters in triplicate. She writes mysteries about small towns that keep their receipts.

chapters.title: The Empty Box
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Called to assess the exhumation of founder Lior Ashford ahead of a land sale, Juniper watches the coffin come up light — and empty. Her memory flashes back to the funeral she attended as a teenager. The beat: unease sharpening into obsession as she notices her mother's signature on the old burial file.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Secrets
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She pulls seven years of archived claims and reconstructs the paper trail: a payout signed by her mother, Ruth, weeks before Ruth's own death. The current mayor warns her off gently, which only confirms something. Beat: grief resurfacing, and the first taste of defiance.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Alibis
chapters.summary: Juniper interviews the four surviving founding families, whose stories align too perfectly — rehearsed down to identical weather details. Only Theo Ashford, Lior's estranged grandson, hesitates and admits he never believed his grandfather left town. Beat: an unlikely alliance begins; loneliness cracks open into cautious trust.

chapters.title: The Night It Rained Sideways
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, interleaved with sensory memory. Using her photographic recall of the funeral, she fixes the timeline: Lior died two days earlier than officially recorded. Someone moved the body. Theo finds a hidden ledger in the Ashford house hinting at offshore transfers. Beat: dread — this was organized, not impulsive.

chapters.title: What Ruth Knew
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Digging into her mother's effects, she finds a torn letter naming 'the four' and warning that Lior planned to dissolve the trust that built the town. Ruth wasn't complicit; she was investigating. Beat: reframing her mother from stranger to ally, fury replacing shame.

chapters.title: A Settlement in an Envelope
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. A lawyer offers her a generous settlement and her mother's sealed personnel file if she signs a confidentiality agreement. She memorizes every page before refusing. That night her office is ransacked — but nothing taken, because everything is in her head. Beat: threat made personal; resolve hardens.

chapters.title: The Fourth Chair
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. He confronts his grandmother, the last living conspirator lucid enough to talk, and learns the fourth family erased itself from records after the murder. Juniper identifies them from a single photograph: the family of the town's beloved sheriff. Beat: betrayal at the heart of the town's mythology.

chapters.title: Where the River Keeps Its Dead
chapters.summary: Juniper and Theo follow the ledger to an abandoned mill on the river, where ground-penetrating radar shows remains matching Lior. They're discovered and nearly killed when someone floods the site; they escape with photographic proof. Beat: terror and exhilaration — the case is now undeniable, and so are they as targets.

chapters.title: Centennial
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. At Witness's centennial gala, with the whole town assembled, she presents the ledger, the radar images, and her memory of every forged signature, while the aging sheriff confesses under the weight of the room's gaze. The founders' descendants turn on each other. Beat: climax — justice spoken aloud where silence was the town's religion.

chapters.title: Belonging
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV, weeks later. The law moves slowly and imperfectly, but the truth is out; Ruth's name is cleared and added to the town memorial beside Lior's restored grave. Theo asks Juniper to help rebuild the Ashford archive — and stay. Beat: resolution — she stops filing the town's secrets and starts keeping its company.
